name: L-phenylalanine
short: In inherited PKU, high maternal phenylalanine in pregnancy is teratogenic (microcephaly, intellectual disability, heart defects); PKU adults had more adverse events on oral phenylalanine than placebo.
text: Phenylalanine is the amino acid that builds up in phenylketonuria (PKU). A review of maternal PKU describes its effects in pregnancy as teratogenic, including intellectual disability (termed mental retardation in the abstract), microcephaly, congenital heart disease and intrauterine growth retardation, at frequencies approaching 75-90% for microcephaly and intellectual disability in untreated pregnancies with high maternal blood phenylalanine, with a dose-response relationship; this review is about raised phenylalanine from the inherited disorder, and the abstract does not discuss supplements. In a randomised, double-blind crossover trial in 30 adults with classical PKU, 4 weeks of oral phenylalanine (reported at 1500-3000 mg a day) was noninferior to placebo for working memory accuracy, and the secondary outcomes (including mood and depression) did not differ significantly except sustained attention, for which the abstract does not say which period did better; adverse events were more frequent during the phenylalanine period, and the abstract does not say what they were. Outside PKU, in a small vitiligo study of 21 patients given L-phenylalanine by mouth with UVA light (10 of whom also applied a 10% L-phenylalanine cream to the vitiligo patches), no side effects were found in either group, and an open trial in 70 people with vitiligo given L-phenylalanine by mouth and as a 10% gel on the skin, with sunlight or UVA lamps and 0.025% clobetasol propionate at night, found no biochemical abnormalities. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
